title: The Lion and the Mouse

sentences.text: A lion was asleep in the warm grass when a mouse ran across his paw.
The lion woke with a growl and set his huge paw over the mouse.
Please let me go, said the mouse. One day I may help you.
The lion laughed because the mouse was tiny, but he lifted his paw.
The mouse darted into the grass and was gone.
Weeks later, hunters left the lion tied in a strong rope net.
He pulled and roared, but the knots held tight.
The mouse heard him, ran to the net, and chewed the rope until it split.
The lion stepped free. The tiny mouse had kept the promise.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: Hunters who cannot find their way in the grass
A lion who learns how to sleep all day
A rope net that nobody is able to open
A small mouse who later helps the lion that let him go

questions.explanation: The lion lets the mouse go, and later the mouse chews the net so the lion can step free. The whole story is about that returned help.

choices.text: The mouse runs across the lion's paw
Hunters tie the lion inside a net
The mouse chews through the rope
The lion steps out and goes free

questions.explanation: At the start, the lion is asleep and the mouse runs over his paw. The net, the chewing, and the escape all come later.

questions.prompt: How does the mouse free the lion?

choices.text: By roaring loudly at the hunters
By chewing the rope until it splits
By digging a tunnel under the net
By calling a much bigger animal

questions.explanation: The story says the mouse chewed the rope until it split. That is the exact way the lion gets out of the net.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original.
